reason: Revision-9 Adversarial and Interdependency were supported after correcting the staged-queue advancement contract. Revision-9 Normalization then confirmed that the generated queue still conflated final completion with inter-stage advancement by rendering an in-progress record under 'Advancement gate' as 'BLOCKED'. Normalization corrected only that representation: the generator now labels the section 'Final completion gate', renders unresolved work as 'OPEN', states that ordered revalidation may continue when current and earlier prerequisites are supported, and retains fail-closed --check behavior for final completion/merge. A regression assertion now protects that terminology. Because update_revalidation_queue.py and its test are governed artifacts included in the artifact-state binding, the correction made all revision-9 semantic gates stale. Revision-9 Normalization therefore receives no credit, review_revision increments to 10, and the ordered semantic chain reopens at Adversarial. Revision-10 Adversarial found no blocking defect under convergence mode. Revision-10 Interdependency then confirmed that the corrected queue/final-completion representation, active change record, stage-order validators, historical identity controls, and workflow form a coherent producer-consumer chain; the queue source hash naturally changes when stage evidence is recorded and is regenerated at the next stage boundary without changing the governed artifact target. Revision-10 Normalization then confirmed that the corrected final-completion/stage-progression vocabulary is consistent across canonical prose, generated queue output, execution terminology, and regression assertions; no material normalization defect remains.

adversarial_convergence.trigger: The separated-pass architecture exceeded the three-retry convergence threshold during revision 8. Revision 10 preserves that stopping policy after a bounded Normalization representation correction.
adversarial_convergence.blocking_rule: Only findings that threaten a declared core invariant, permit false credit or protected-control bypass, materially overstate assurance, invalidate required mapped/downstream conclusions, or expose a genuinely new reusable attack class may invalidate the next Adversarial pass.
adversarial_convergence.nonblocking_rule: Minor documentation, redundant hardening, low-impact edge cases, optional diagnostics, and other observations that do not threaten the core invariants are recorded or deferred and do not cause a restart.
core_invariants: No false semantic stage or execution-pass credit can be accepted by the governed completion path.
Required separated/subdivided execution order and bounded handoff chaining cannot be bypassed by backfilling multiple passes into one durable execution state.
A durably completed pass or stage plan cannot be replaced, mutated, replayed, or redone without the required review-revision reopening semantics and new execution identities.
Current and partial execution evidence cannot be accepted under a stale review revision, stale gate, or stale governed artifact state.
Historical/base-state evidence and the closed exemption boundary prevent reuse or omission that would falsely legitimize current execution evidence.
Repository checks and records do not claim to prove an actual host message/context or isolation boundary when the host supplies no independently trustworthy boundary identity.
adversarial_convergence.next_pass_requirement: Classify every new material Adversarial observation as blocking or non-blocking against these invariants before making any correction.
